source.title: Decoupling Knowledge from Memorization: Retrieval-augmented Prompt Learning
source.authors: Xiang Chen; Lei Li; Ning-Yu Zhang; Xiao-Zhuan Liang; Shu-Min Deng; Chuan-Qi Tan; Fei Huang; Luo Si; Hua-Jun Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no evident truncation or garbling affecting the reported findings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results on retrieval-augmented prompting and memorization in pretrained language models for NLP classification and extraction tasks, a setting outside the mapped versions’ specified networks and benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports retrieval-augmented prompt-learning results and analyzes memorization scores. Its ablations and representation comparisons measure retrieval components, not the architecture, optimizer, batch size, regularization, model size, or sharpness claims in V1–V8. Hyperparameter sweeps select retrieval settings and are not results on a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study measures retrieval-augmented NLP performance and influence-based memorization scores, neither of which tests V1–V8. Its closest connection is V8, but it does not remove highly memorized examples, retrain, and compare test accuracy with matched random removals. A new application setting alone does not justify T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: RetroPrompt improves performance in few-shot, zero-shot, fully supervised, and cross-domain evaluations, and the authors interpret lower memorization scores as reduced reliance on parametric memorization. That interpretation is not a causal demonstration that reducing memorization improves generalization. Their zero-shot setting uses unlabeled training data with pseudo labels for retrieval.
record.recipe_differences: Retrieval-augmented prompt learning for pretrained language models; it uses retrieval during input construction, training, and prediction and analyzes memorization scores rather than testing the mapped interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports retrieval hyperparameter sensitivity: performance changes with β, λ, and k; the best λ differs between 16-shot and zero-shot MR, and zero-shot MR performance improves with k until k=256.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 3 reports mean SST-2 memorization scores of 4.597 for fine-tuning, 0.121 for LM-BFF, and 0.032 for RetroPrompt. These are influence-based self-memorization scores, without a removal-and-retraining test of held-out accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrieval-augmented prompt learning can yield lower measured self-memorization scores than fine-tuning or ordinary prompt learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Task-performance comparisons, cross-domain evaluations, and retrieval ablations show benefits of the proposed retrieval method. Table 4 reports lower performance after removing each retrieval component on all five evaluated datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retrieval augmentation can improve downstream NLP performance, with gains depending on its components and retrieval settings.

record.problems: The mapped versions’ outcomes are not measured. Memorization evidence is a scoring comparison on SST-2 rather than a causal removal-and-retraining test; some reported retrieval-sensitivity results are figures without exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify for V1–V8: reported task-performance comparisons and retrieval ablations concern a different claim subject and intervention. Table 3's memorization-score values also do not measure any mapped version; its role is summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; all reported experiments use AdamW.
Large versus small batches under matched epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Listed batch sizes are tuning choices, without comparative results.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the qualifying result rows and verdict labels empty is appropriate. The omitted results are declared in rows_left_out and do not bear on a listed version. The citation to Feldman and Zhang and the use of a related memorization score do not constitute a test of V8.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-network comparison.
All experiments use AdamW; no adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or large-batch generalization-gap analysis.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison.
Memorization scores are analyzed, but the study does not remove high-scoring examples and retrain against random removals to measure test-accuracy effects.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
